newsitem.title: USA: Mitsubishi Electric aims offering Internet TV in 97. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Electric aims offering Internet TV in 97. [CORRECTED 19:00 GMT]

text.p: Mitsubishi Electric Corp's Mitsubishi Consumer Electronics America Inc said Wednesday it plans to bring a television with Internet capabilities called DiamondWeb to market as early as next summer. (Corrects company name in headline and first paragraph to Mitsubishi Electric from Mitsubishi Corp and changes day of week to Wednesday from Thursday).
Mitsubishi did not release price estimates, but said the initial debut will focus on televisions with large screens measuring up to 40 inches.
Gateway 2000 was the first company to offer television with similar computer capabilities. Its Destination PC/TV, which was launched in March, has a 31-inch screen and starts at about $3,999.

DiamondWeb would have access to the World Wide Web and other Internet services, a single remote, strong graphic and audio features, according to Mitsubishi. It would access the Web through Mitsubishi's WebView feature.

"DiamondWeb TV will present the Internet as just another channel to the user -- switching to the Web will be as easy as changing channels," said Jack Osborn, president MCEA. "We expect that within a few years, large screen sets without this capacity will disappear altogether."
The televisions would use Motorola Inc's MPC801 Power PC microprocessor and Microware Systems Corp's software operating system.
